correctness.rationale: The closed-neighborhood criterion DD(a,b) is derived exactly. The partition excess lower bound e>=min(r-1,4) is proved by counting available non-singleton vertices and two distinct supporting partners; known hub/bridge constructions attain it. For r>=6, e=4 forces exactly two mixed bridge triples. For r<=5, s>2(r-1) the B-singleton partner is either a whole A-shore or a mixed (a,1) block; the remaining excess forces a split hub or (at r=5) bridge triples. All nine uncovered bounded pairs are certified by complete multiset enumeration of excess compositions and occupancy pairs with direct partner predicates. Counts follow from labeled selections. VERIFY_OK tests 68 parameter pairs and 4 independent labeled-partition cases.

value.rationale: Full equality-structure classification and labeled multiplicity for a natural infinite biclique family whose scalar optimum was known. The r=5 emergence of two bridge triples induces a structural polynomial-degree transition (linear vs cubic) not implied by the scalar bound or by arbitrary relabeling. Supports enumerative work on extremal coalition configurations; excludes unrelated/nonoptimal structures.
